title: Hymn 3, sound: gagan mai thaal
hookLine: gagan mai thaal rav chand deepak bane (Dhanasri M1, ang 13)

lines: IT OPENS ON ONE WORD: SKY.
cards: Lie on your back outside on a clear night and the sky stops being a ceiling. It becomes a bowl, curved over you from edge to edge. Sohila's third hymn starts from that angle.
It's Guru Nanak's, in Raag Dhanasri, on Ang 13, and its very first word is gagan, the sky. Its first line is a picture you could almost hold in two hands.

teach.b: Here's the opening: gagan mai thaal, rav chand deepak bane. Word by word. Gagan: the sky, the whole vault of the heavens.
Thaal: a platter, the round metal tray you'd carry food or offerings on. Rav: the sun; you met it yesterday as sooraj, and rav is another old name for it.

teach.h: RAV AND CHAND: SUN AND MOON.

teach.b: Deepak: lamps, the little flames set on a tray. Bane: have become. So: the sky is the platter, and the sun and moon have become its lamps.

The line keeps going, and we'll open the rest tomorrow, but this much is already a whole picture. Somebody is holding a tray of light. The tray is the sky; the lamps are the two great lights we live by.
Notice how the week has built to this. The first hymn began in a house. The second walked through the six schools and ended at the sun.
Now the third sets the sun and moon on a platter, like an offering. Sohila keeps widening the frame: a doorway, a marketplace, the calendar, now the whole sky.
And the words are plain: gagan, thaal, rav, chand, deepak, each an object you could point to.

how: Sikhs recite this hymn nightly as the third of Kirtan Sohila's five, and in many gurdwaras it is also sung on its own in the evening, often called the Aarti.

o: the sky, the whole vault of the heavens
a round tray carried with lamps on it
the earth, the ground beneath your feet

games.q: the first line of hymn 3 — tap the pairs.

s: Sohila's third hymn is by Guru Nanak
gagan mai thaal means the sky is full of thunder
it means the sky is the platter.
in the line, the sun and moon become lamps
rav chand deepak bane: sun and moon have become the lamps.

games.q: Guru Nanak looks up at the sky. what does the first line make of it?
o: a platter, with the sun and moon as its lamps.
an empty space with nothing in it.
games.why: gagan mai thaal, rav chand deepak bane: the sky is a tray of offering, and sun and moon are its lamps.

practice: Say the line slowly, one word at a time: gagan, mai, thaal, rav, chand, deepak, bane. Say it again and picture a round tray held up in both hands with two flames on it, then let the tray grow until it's the size of the sky.
Rest in that picture, and if you pray, say the line once more.

wordCard.voice: Gagan, the sky: Sohila's third hymn, by Guru Nanak in Raag Dhanasri, the sky is the platter, and the sun and moon have become its lamps.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: gagan, the sky; the first word of Sohila's third hymn.
